headword: {感覚神経|かんかくしんけい}

definitions.explanation: A nerve that carries signals from sensory receptors (in the skin, eyes, ears, etc.) to the brain and spinal cord, enabling the perception of touch, pain, temperature, sight, hearing, and other sensations.

examples.japanese: {感覚神経|かんかくしんけい}が{痛|いた}みを{伝|つた}える。
{感覚神経|かんかくしんけい}が{損傷|そんしょう}すると、しびれが{生|しょう}じる。
examples.english: When sensory nerves are damaged, numbness occurs.

examples.japanese: {指先|ゆびさき}には{感覚神経|かんかくしんけい}が{密集|みっしゅう}しているため、わずかな{触|ふ}れ{方|かた}の{違|ちが}いも{感|かん}じ{取|と}れる。
examples.english: Because sensory nerves are densely concentrated in the fingertips, we can detect even slight differences in touch.

notes:
A compound of {感覚|かんかく} (sensation, sense) and {神経|しんけい} (nerve). A basic anatomy term used in biology and medicine. Sensory nerves are one of the two main types of peripheral nerves, the other being {運動神経|うんどうしんけい} (motor nerves).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {感覚神経|かんかくしんけい}の{障害|しょうがい}: sensory nerve disorder
- {感覚神経|かんかくしんけい}が{麻痺|まひ}する: sensory nerves become numb
- {末梢|まっしょう}{感覚神経|かんかくしんけい}: peripheral sensory nerve

RELATED WORDS:
- {運動神経|うんどうしんけい}: motor nerve — carries signals from the brain to muscles for movement
- {自律神経|じりつしんけい}: autonomic nerve — controls involuntary functions like heartbeat and digestion
- {末梢神経|まっしょうしんけい}: peripheral nerve — nerves outside the brain and spinal cord
